To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RAFT1 protein, which interacts with the drug complex rapamycin FK506 binding protein (FKBP12), contains phosphatidylinositide 4 kinase activity.

the immunosuppressants rapamycin and FK506 inhibit mammalian and yeast cell growth by interacting with the small proteins FK506 binding protein (FKBP12) and FKBP12-rapamycin associated protein (FRAP), respectively, which are members of the TOR family.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the molecular mechanism of action of the immunosuppressants FK506 and rapamycin.
the identification of the molecular targets of the immunosuppressive drugs FK506 and rapamycin.
the molecular mechanisms by which the immunosuppressants, FK506 and rapamycin, inhibit T cell proliferation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the RAFT1 protein contains a domain with homology to several PI 4 and 4 3 kinases, but that this domain has not been directly shown to be a PI 4 kinase.
the RAFT1 and TOR1/2 proteins are not PI 4 kinase homologs.
the PI 4-kinase activity of RAFT1 is not affected by rapamycin and FK506 binding protein 12.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RAFT1 protein is a PI 4 kinase and the rapamycin/FKBP12 drug complex inhibits a downstream target.

the RAFT1 protein is a phosphatidylinositide kinase, and that it is not a target for the immunosuppressants rapamycin and FK506, but instead is an important regulator of cell cycle progression in mammalian cells.
the RAFT1 protein has a PI 4 kinase domain and is a potential target of rapamycin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RAFT proteins are not PI 4 kinases and that their role in the PI 4/3 kinase family is still unknown.
RAFT1/ FRAP proteins are not PI 4 kinases, and that the PI 4 and 5 kinases, PI4KII and PI4KIII, are the likely targets for the immunosuppressants.
